messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(L_t\) be the length of the red-endpoint stick after \(t\) minutes, with \(L_0=1\).

Before minute \(t\), there are exactly \(t\) sticks total. Since there is always exactly one red-endpoint stick, the probability he picks it is \(1/t\).

Conditional on the previous red stick length \(L\):

- With probability \(1/t\), it is broken, so its new length is \(L/2\).
- With probability \(1-1/t\), it is not broken, so its length remains \(L\).

Thus

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_t \mid L_{t-1}=L]
= \frac{1}{t}\cdot \frac{L}{2} + \left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)L
= L\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right).
\]

Taking expectations,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_t]
= \mathbb{E}[L_{t-1}]\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right).
\]

So after 5 minutes,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
= \prod_{t=1}^5 \left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)
= \frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac78\cdot\frac9{10}.
\]

Compute:

\[
\frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac78\cdot\frac9{10}
= \frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
